 Brad Pitt's 2014 War Movie 'Fury,' Hailed for Its Battle Scenes, Will Hit Netflix Nov. 1
 Men's Journal Follow Melody McCune Add to Preferred Sources Fri, October 30, 2026 at 3:12 PM UTC Brad Pitt's 2014 War Movie 'Fury,' Hailed for Its Battle Scenes, Will Hit Netflix Nov. 1 Brad Pitt has a decades-long career of starring in top-notch films from prestige directors, from comedies and dramas to period pieces. In 2014, he headlined one particular war movie that took the box office by storm—and on Nov. 1, it'll undoubtedly do the same on Netflix .
 About 'Fury'
 For the uninitiated, Fury follows Pitt as tank commander Don "Wardaddy" Collier, who "makes tough decisions as he and his crew fight their way across Germany in April 1945."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In addition to Pitt, Fury stars Shia LaBeouf as Boyd "Bible" Swan, Logan Lerman as Norman Ellison, Michael Peña as Trini "Gordo" Garcia, Jon Bernthal as Grady "Coon-Ass" Travis, and Jason Isaacs as Captain Waggoner. David Ayer directed from his own script. Ayer derived inspiration from Belton Y. Cooper 's 1998 memoir Death Traps: The Survival of an American Armored Division in World War II .
 The actors underwent four months of intense training. They even participated in a Navy SEAL boot camp. Ayer pushed them to the brink, too, urging them to physically fight each other, spew vitriol, and live together in a tank where they also ate and went to the bathroom. Talk about going method. The filmmaker remarked that he was " ruthless as a director " and would do whatever it took to "get what I want."
 Fury premiered on Oct. 17, 2014, in the U.S. It was a massive commercial hit, grossing $211.8 million on a budget of $68-80 million. It skyrocketed to No. 1 at the box office and became Ayer's most successful movie. 
 Critically, Fury received mixed reviews. The San Francisco Chronicle hailed it as "a great movie" because it "lets you know you're in safe hands from the beginning." Film critic James Berardinelli called it " memorable ," adding that it accurately depicts "the horrors of war without reveling in the depravity of man."
 Advertisement Advertisement Fury boasts 75% on the Rotten Tomatoes Tomatometer and 84% on the Popcornmeter. The review aggregator's critics' consensus reads thusly: "Overall, Fury is a well-acted, suitably raw depiction of the horrors of war that offers visceral battle scenes but doesn't quite live up to its larger ambitions."
 Kicking Off Netflix's November Streaming Slate
 You can stream the Brad Pitt hit when it arrives on Netflix on Nov. 1.
